column1: # Where this fork names or defines something differently from typetools.
# Used by checker/bin-devel/typetools-import-check.py and shown in docs/developer/README-eisop.md.
# Columns, separated by tabs: kind, scope, typetools, eisop, since, reason.
#   kind: "collision" = the same name means something different here, so an import can silently
#         change behavior; "rename" = a different name for the same thing; "api" = a different
#         design (see reason); "file" = the code of a typetools file is in other files here.
#   typetools / eisop: a method or class name, as it appears in code; "-" if there is none.
#         For "file", typetools is a path and eisop a comma-separated list of paths, "-" if the
#         code has no counterpart here.  A path without a slash is in the directory of the
#         typetools path; a path ending in a slash means all files in that directory.  A typetools
#         path ending in a slash maps every file below it to the same name below the eisop path.
#   since: the typetools release (or this fork's decision) the entry applies from.

column6: typetools 3.55.0 (#7594) renamed getEffectiveAnnotation*, hasEffectiveAnnotation*, getEffectiveAnnotations to getAnnotation*, hasAnnotation*, getAnnotations. Here getAnnotation*, hasAnnotation*, and getAnnotations() keep meaning the annotations on that type itself, as in javac.

Typetools 3.54.0 writes expected error keys as [key]; the test harness here accepts both forms, so tests need not be converted. Typetools' rework of TestDiagnostic (message to key, -Aonelinemsg instead of -Anomsgtext) is not imported.

The modules are compiled for Java 8, where the since element does not exist; typetools' #7572 converted the comments to it. Write the date as a comment.

Its expected javap output holds a constant-pool index that differs between JDK 8, 11, and 17+.

This fork split the class when it separated the Initialization Checker from the Nullness Checker. The abstract superclass InitializationParentAnnotatedTypeFactory, shared with the field-access subchecker, holds the type and tree annotators, the qualifier hierarchy, and the type-frame helpers; the subclass InitializationAnnotatedTypeFactory holds the parts that use the flow analysis; InitializationFieldAccessTreeAnnotator types field accesses. Typetools' field-invariant methods have no counterpart. The import of typetools 3.51.1 dropped the source hunk of fc3a55d3521b because of this split.
